summaryActionTitle: Turn the rhythm into one concrete action
patternChoiceTitle: What the pattern shows, and what remains yours
patternChoiceBody: MING does not treat birth data as a command. It translates traditional structure into observable tendencies, then gives the final choice back to you.
beforeDecisionSubtitle: Turn “this feels accurate” into a checkable next step.
careerReportIntro: This report separates career structure into drive, work environment, advantage scenarios, risk boundaries, and practical actions. It does not decide which job you should take or promise outcomes. It helps you see how you create value and where clear rules are needed.
wealthReportIntro: This report does not forecast income or claim whether someone will become rich. It separates opportunity access, resource retention, decision impulses, investment boundaries, and risk dispersion so financial intentions become recordable and reviewable actions.
relationshipReportIntro: This report does not judge relationship outcomes or make emotional decisions for the user. It observes support, pressure boundaries, communication rhythm, and responsibility sharing so vague feelings can become specific conversations.
careerPracticalBody: Translate career goals into three layers: what you can deliver this week, who needs to recognize it this month, and what ability or case should remain three months later. Write an acceptance standard for each goal, such as a proposal, work sample, review, or reusable process. This turns abstract career rhythm into progress that can be checked.
wealthPracticalBody: Build a simple money decision table: opportunity name, expected input, tolerable loss, validation period, exit condition, and review date. Fill it before major decisions. Even when outcomes are uncertain, the thinking process is preserved, making it possible to learn whether you recognized an opportunity or were pushed by emotion and external stimulation.
relationshipPracticalBody: Use a low-conflict communication format: state the fact, name the feeling, make a specific request, then confirm whether the other side can do it. For example: 'This happened three times recently, I feel more pressure, I hope we can confirm it one day earlier next time. Is that workable?' This is easier to solve than judging the other person directly.
actionChecklist: Define the current goal as one deliverable, not only a wish
Clarify responsibility boundaries, acceptance standards, and feedback rhythm before important cooperation
Record real output weekly and separate busyness from progress
Review opportunity, cost, resistance, and next choice monthly
In pressure years, reduce scope and avoid too many parallel tasks
Turn reusable experience into work samples, processes, or cases
wealthActionChecklist: Track income, spending, and opportunity cost separately instead of keeping one vague account
Set a budget cap, validation period, and review date for major input
When opportunities multiply, compare clarity, payback cycle, and exit conditions first
Wait one night before any large decision, then reassess with a table
Do not turn short-term emotion, face pressure, or external stimulation into long-term financial judgment
Improve only one financial habit each month; prioritize steady execution
relationshipActionChecklist: State expectations, responsibilities, and boundaries in concrete language instead of making the other side guess
Confirm shared goals before discussing responsibility and commitment
In conflict, restate facts before naming feelings, and avoid labeling the other person directly
Turn requests into executable actions, including timing, frequency, and specific support
Review whether communication cost and support remain balanced
If repeated communication fails, reduce energy loss first before deciding whether to continue investing

annualReportTitle: Next Five Years Pro Rhythm Report
annualReportIntro: This report combines natal traits with annual-flow structure to compare relative yearly rhythm. It is a timing map, not an outcome forecast. It helps decide when to test, when to limit commitments, and when to review.

annualFocus.career_progress: Concentrate on clear deliverables, career progress, and visible results.
annualFocus.wealth_boundaries: Separate opportunity, cash flow, and input boundaries; test before expanding.
annualFocus.relationship_communication: Prioritize expectations, responsibility, cooperation, and communication rhythm.
annualFocus.execution_rhythm: Stabilize plans, reduce parallel tasks, and establish fixed review points.

annualCaution.avoid_scattered_goals: Avoid scattered goals and repeated direction changes that prevent accumulation.
annualCaution.avoid_unbounded_input: Avoid continued input without a budget, deadline, or exit condition.
annualCaution.avoid_unspoken_expectations: Avoid relying on guesses in relationships; make concrete requests explicit.
annualCaution.avoid_overcommitment: Avoid excessive commitments and overloaded schedules; finish critical work first.

monthlyCompassIntro: The Monthly Compass does not label months as good or bad. It combines natal traits with the monthly stem-branch structure and identifies the strongest relative shift. Each month offers one focus, one boundary, and one testable action for real-world review.

monthlyFocus.make_visible_progress: Concentrate on one result that can be seen and evaluated.
monthlyFocus.test_before_expanding: Validate the opportunity at low cost before expanding commitment.
monthlyFocus.clarify_expectations: State expectations, responsibilities, and requests clearly instead of relying on guesses.
monthlyFocus.build_repeatable_rhythm: Build one stable rhythm that can be repeated every week.

monthlyBoundary.limit_scattered_goals: Limit the number of simultaneous goals and protect attention.
monthlyBoundary.set_cost_and_exit_limits: Set a budget, deadline, and exit condition before committing resources.
monthlyBoundary.replace_guessing_with_requests: Replace hints and assumptions with explicit requests.
monthlyBoundary.protect_recovery_and_focus: Protect recovery and deep-work time; avoid overcommitting.

monthlyExperiment.ship_one_visible_result: Deliver one visible result before month-end and record external feedback.
monthlyExperiment.run_one_small_validation: Run one minimum test with a written cost ceiling and success criterion.
monthlyExperiment.hold_one_clear_conversation: Complete one low-conflict conversation: fact, feeling, request, confirmation.
monthlyExperiment.repeat_one_weekly_system: Repeat the same weekly system for four weeks and track completion rather than mood.

monthlyReflection.reflect_career: Which activity became a visible result, and which remained only busyness?
monthlyReflection.reflect_wealth: Which input was validated, and which was driven by emotion?
monthlyReflection.reflect_relationship: Which misunderstanding came from an expectation that was never spoken?
monthlyReflection.reflect_stability: Which rhythm supported steady progress, and which commitment consumed the most?
